description: Hi. We are Team HyperNova, a group of Sri Lankan space enthusiasts who are looking to deliver something exceptional through this event.
summary: "LunarSkyline": a web application that abstracts away the complexities of finding the viability of landing at a specific location and time on the moon, to give a simplified user experience for mission planners.
details:
"LunarSkyline" is a web application that extracts away the complexities of existing tools to provide a simplified user experience to whoever is using it to plan missions to the lunar South pole.

The tool gives a very intuitive user interface to select the desired location and date/time. The location can be selected either from a drop-down that provides names of some known locations or the user can input custom longitude and latitude coordinates. Additionally, the user can select the time window they are planning to explore and the period of time where the expedition can tolerate blackouts. Then, the tool uses existing JPL Horizons system to get necessary information about the location of the Sun and the Earth, and the terrain information from LOLA models for that input combination and analyzes the viability of landing.

Then, it displays the status of viability with color indicators and additional vital details such as the percentage of time where the Sun and the Earth are available. There is a section depicting the trajectory the Sun and the Earth is moving for the selected time window clearly when they go behind ridges. This is supported by two view: 1. a 360 degree panoramic view of the horizon and 2. a sky dome view of how the rover sees the sky. These visuals give instant feedback to the user on the evolution of the situation in the time neighborhood. Additionally, there is a third view showing the elevation of these objects during the time frame.

The significance of "LunarSkyline" when there is potentially many other NASA tools is that this provides a simplified view to the mission planners who may have a non-technical background. We believe the existing tools are too complex and complicated to use for instant mission planning and once someone narrows down the combinations with this tool, they can then dive into more detailed tools. The key point is that this tool is built on top of the existing tools to provide a simplified abstraction. So, accuracy and performance are not affected. As a result, we believe NASA personnel can easily adopt this tool into their stack.

The tool has a few additional features such as comparing two or more scenarios side-by-side and the option to choose the best one, and finding the rocket trajectory and launch data once a viable landing is confirmed.

We believe our tool provides a unique solution that helps NASA mission planners to easily navigate through the entire pipeline, starting with adding a potential landing site, evaluate the viability, consider the suggested alternatives, compare many landing options at once, and analyze rocket trajectory.

The frontend is developed as a React app with a backend running Python. The backend uses LOLA models to generate terrain landscape and query the official NASA tools. Code is written with Cursor with the help of some AI/SI models.
dataRefs: LOLA (NASA GSFC Planetary Geodesy Data Archive)
